Subject: RE: Activation failing for GlacierWorks — possible header encoding issue (case 5543)

Hi Ben / team,

Thanks for the detailed reproducer. We've investigated case 5543. Root cause: some client mail relays that GlacierWorks' provider uses were normalizing header encodings when the From/Subject contained mixed punctuation (em-dash) and non-ASCII characters. Our outbound mailer was defaulting to an older mail library in this tenant path that emitted an uncommon charset token under certain templating conditions; the receiving relay then coerced the Subject/headers and in a subset of messages the URL query portion was affected.

Mitigation we've applied:
- Reissued a corrected invite to onboarding@glacierworks.com with an explicit UTF-8 Content-Type and quoted-printable encoding for the Subject.
- We deployed a hotfix to the invite generator to explicitly percent-encode tokens and to normalize the display name to NFC form before rendering.

Case ID: COUPA-5543. You can find the support summary here: https://support.coupa.com/cases/5543

Please confirm once GlacierWorks receives and can use the new invite. We can also manually activate the account if the customer prefers.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Coupa Support Engineer
